note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in UT.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Logan Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway (2002)
byways.where: US-89 from 1500 East in Logan to SR-30 in Garden City; Cache and Rich counties

facts.fact: The lower canyon walls expose about 500 million years of geologic history in fossil-bearing formations.
The byway follows the Logan River from Logan to Garden City past limestone cliffs and tops out at a view over Bear Lake.
Runs on US-89 from 1500 East in Logan to SR-30 in Garden City; designated a National Scenic Byway June 13, 2002.

byways.name: Bear Lake Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: US-89 from the Idaho line to SR-30, and SR-30 from Garden City to Laketown; Rich County

facts.fact: Designated in 1990 as the Laketown Scenic Byway; extended and renamed in 2002 to take in the US-89 segment north of Garden City.
SR-30 runs along the shore of turquoise Bear Lake between Laketown and Garden City, a town known for raspberry milkshakes in summer.

byways.name: Ogden River Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-39 from the mouth of Ogden Canyon to the forest boundary near milepost 48, with a loop around Pineview Reservoir on SR-158; Weber County

facts.fact: The road runs up an extremely narrow canyon from Ogden and comes out at Pineview Reservoir near Huntsville.
Its high point near Monte Cristo Summit is nearly 9,000 feet, and the highest stretch is closed in winter, usually December through April.
Ogden Canyon is a quartzite gorge.

byways.name: Big Cottonwood Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-190 from SR-210 at the canyon mouth to the Brighton Loop; Salt Lake County

facts.fact: The 15-mile drive leads to two four-season ski resorts and to Silver Lake and its visitor center.
The canyon holds old mining country; Solitude and Brighton sit near the top; watershed rules prohibit domestic animals.

byways.name: Little Cottonwood Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-210 from SR-209 to the end of state maintenance near Alta; Salt Lake County

facts.fact: The canyon is glacially carved, lies in the Salt Lake City watershed and is closed to pets.
Pioneers quarried granite blocks for the Salt Lake Temple at the canyon mouth; climbers use 400-foot granite walls; Albion Basin is known for spring and early summer wildflowers.

byways.name: Provo Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: US-189 from SR-52 in Orem/Provo to SR-113 near Charleston, then SR-113 through Midway to US-40 in Heber City; Utah and Wasatch counties

facts.fact: Bridal Veil Falls, a double-cataract waterfall, can be seen from the road; Deer Creek Reservoir lies at the top of the canyon; the Heber Valley Railroad runs tours.
Realigned in 2003 from the eastern part of US-189 onto SR-113.

byways.name: Mirror Lake Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-150 from SR-32 in Kamas to the Wyoming line; Summit County

facts.fact: From Kamas the road passes farm and ranch land, then rises into forested mountains with many access points to the High Uintas Wilderness.
It crests at Bald Mountain Pass, 10,715 feet, Utah's highest paved road.
The corridor is a Forest Service recreation fee area (3-day pass $10).

byways.review: Catalog line is the Utah section only; the byway continues into Wyoming as WY-150.

byways.name: Morgan-Parleys Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway (designated December 11, 2017)
byways.where: SR-66 from I-84 in Morgan to SR-65, then SR-65 to I-80 in Parleys Canyon; Morgan and Salt Lake counties

facts.fact: SR-66 from I-84 in Morgan to SR-65, and SR-65 south to I-80 in Parleys Canyon; designated December 11, 2017.
The route passes East Canyon State Park, follows parts of the Mormon, California and Pony Express trails, and SR-65 south of Big Mountain closes for about six months each winter and spring.

byways.name: Great Salt Lake Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway (designated 2002 as Great Salt Lake Legacy Parkway Scenic Byway, renamed 2018)
byways.where: SR-67 (Legacy Parkway) from I-215 to I-15 at Farmington; extended 2018 along the West Davis Corridor to SR-127 and Antelope Island Marina; Davis County

facts.fact: Designated May 16, 2002 as the Great Salt Lake Legacy Parkway Scenic Byway; renamed Great Salt Lake Scenic Byway and extended in 2018 along the West Davis Corridor and SR-127 to the Antelope Island Marina.
The parkway (SR-67) gives views of Great Salt Lake, whose shores are a stopover for millions of migratory birds each spring and fall.

byways.review: Catalog name and line are the original 12-mile Legacy Parkway (SR-67). The state renamed it Great Salt Lake Scenic Byway in 2018 and extended it along the West Davis Corridor and SR-127 to Antelope Island; the UDOT layer ('Great Salt Lake Scenic Byway', about 43 miles) includes the extension.

byways.name: Markagunt High Plateau Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-14 from SR-130 in Cedar City to US-89 at Long Valley Junction; Iron and Kane counties

facts.fact: SR-14 runs 40 miles from Cedar City to Long Valley Junction through Cedar Canyon and the Dixie National Forest, topping out near 9,900 feet.
The road climbs a narrow canyon looking into the Ashdown Gorge Wilderness, then crosses ancient lava fields and passes the Navajo Lake overlook and Duck Creek Village.
Navajo Lake is drained by sinkholes where inflowing water disappears into the ground.

byways.name: Cedar Breaks Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-148 from SR-14 through Cedar Breaks National Monument to SR-143; Iron County

facts.fact: SR-148 runs about six miles from SR-14 past the Cedar Breaks visitor center to SR-143, between 9,900 and 10,500 feet; it closes from about mid-November to late May and becomes a groomed snowmobile and ski trail.
The amphitheater is more than 2,000 feet deep and three miles from rim to rim.

byways.name: Brian Head-Panguitch Lake Scenic Byway (Utah's Patchwork Parkway)
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway as Utah's Patchwork Parkway (2009)
byways.where: SR-143 from the I-15 south Parowan interchange to US-89 in Panguitch; Iron and Garfield counties

facts.fact: In a winter storm in 1864, Mormon pioneers crossed this route by laying handmade quilts on the snow to keep from sinking.

The road climbs from Parowan past Brian Head to a 10,400-foot summit, then descends through aspen and lava fields past Panguitch Lake; the Parowan to Brian Head grade reaches 13 percent and is not recommended for RVs.
State designation is Brian Head-Panguitch Lake Scenic Byway; national designation as Utah's Patchwork Parkway October 16, 2009.

byways.review: The state rule still calls this road the Brian Head-Panguitch Lake Scenic Byway; it was nationally designated as Utah's Patchwork Parkway in 2009.

byways.name: Kolob Fingers Road Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: Kolob Canyons Road (National Park Service) from I-15 Exit 40 to the Kolob Canyon (Timber Creek) Overlook; Iron and Washington counties

facts.fact: A five-mile scenic drive in the Kolob Canyons district of Zion, at I-15 Exit 40, where narrow parallel box canyons are cut into 2,000-foot cliff walls.
The road climbs over 1,000 feet and ends at the Timber Creek Overlook.
The park entrance fee is required even if you are not stopping.
The road climbs on distinctive red asphalt switchbacks among the park's cliffs.

byways.name: Zion Park Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway; the section from SR-17 in La Verkin to the East Rim Trail Road is the Zion National Scenic Byway (2021)
byways.where: SR-9 from I-15 near Hurricane to US-89 at Mount Carmel Junction; Washington and Kane counties

facts.fact: State designation covers SR-9 from I-15 to US-89; the national byway (designated January 19, 2021) is the section from SR-17 to the East Rim Trail Road.
SR-9 runs through Rockville and Springdale into Zion National Park to the east entrance; the park entrance fee applies even to through traffic.
Cyclists are not allowed through the Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. The UDOT layer draws both 'Zion Park Scenic Byway' (state, whole SR-9) and 'Zion National Scenic Byway' (the national section); use the state value for the full line.

byways.name: Mt. Carmel Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: US-89 from the Kanab north city limit to SR-12 near Bryce Canyon; Kane and Garfield counties

facts.fact: Follows US-89 for 60 miles between SR-12 near Bryce Canyon National Park and Kanab, through red rock canyons and open valleys.
The road crosses the Markagunt Plateau and the Sevier River valley and descends the Pink, Gray, White and Vermilion cliffs of the Grand Staircase to Kanab.

byways.name: Beaver Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-153 from SR-160 in Beaver to the end of pavement near Elk Meadows (Eagle Point); Beaver County

facts.fact: Highway 153 climbs about 17 miles from Beaver into the Tushar Mountains and Fishlake National Forest to Eagle Point Ski Area, rising 4,000 feet past mountain mahogany, ponderosa pine and four hydroelectric plants.
The Tushars are the remains of stratovolcanoes active about 24 million years ago; Beaver was the birthplace of Butch Cassidy.

byways.name: Fishlake Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-25 and county roads FAS-2554 and FAS-3268 (Fremont River Road) from SR-24 past Fish Lake and Johnson Valley Reservoir to SR-72; Sevier and Wayne counties

facts.fact: Fish Lake, Utah's largest natural mountain lake, lies in a down-faulted valley at about 8,843 feet and is 5.5 miles long, known for lake trout over 20 pounds.
Johnson Valley Reservoir, north of the lake, is the source of the Fremont River.
Designated in 1990 on SR-25; extended in 1992 along the Fremont River Road to SR-72.

byways.name: Highway 12, A Journey Through Time Scenic Byway (Scenic Byway 12)
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway; All-American Road (2002)
byways.where: SR-12 from US-89 near Panguitch to SR-24 near Torrey; Garfield and Wayne counties

facts.fact: Scenic Byway 12 runs 124 miles from US-89 near Panguitch, with interpretive sites at Red Canyon, Bryce Canyon, Cannonville, Anasazi State Park and Escalante.
The road passes through two red arches in Red Canyon and follows the Hogback between Escalante and Boulder, where the land drops away into canyons on both sides, before crossing Boulder Mountain.
Designated All-American Road June 13, 2002.

byways.name: Capitol Reef Country Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-24 from SR-72 in Loa to SR-95 in Hanksville; Wayne County

facts.fact: Highway 24 runs about 75 miles from the Fremont River valley at Loa and Bicknell through the Waterpocket Fold to Hanksville, passing the pioneer orchards of Fruita and Fremont Culture petroglyphs.
There are no gas stations or stores for the 50 miles between Torrey and Hanksville; east of the park the road crosses gray Mancos Shale badlands near Caineville below Factory Butte.

byways.name: Flaming Gorge-Uintas Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway (1998)
byways.where: US-191 from US-40 in Vernal to the Wyoming line, SR-44 to Manila and SR-43 to the Wyoming line; Uintah and Daggett counties

facts.fact: The byway crosses the Ashley National Forest between Vernal and Manila, with a segment over Flaming Gorge Dam to the Wyoming line; its theme is 'Wildlife Through the Ages' with 14 interpretive sites.
Bighorn sheep can be seen on the rocks above Sheep Creek, whose cottonwoods and willows hold more species of migrating songbirds than any other spot in Utah.
The formations along the route span some 770 million years of geologic history.

byways.name: Indian Canyon Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway (also part of the Dinosaur Diamond National Scenic Byway)
byways.where: US-191 from US-6 near Helper to US-40 in Duchesne; Carbon and Duchesne counties

facts.fact: Begins in Duchesne on US-191 and crosses colorful terrain between the Uintah Basin and the San Rafael Swell near Price, through steep rock formations and conifer and aspen forest.
US-191 from US-6 near Helper to US-40 in Duchesne; the Dinosaur Diamond National Scenic Byway includes the Indian Canyon State Scenic Byway.

byways.review: The UDOT layer has no separate row; the road is drawn within the 'Dinosaur Diamond Scenic Byway' rows.

byways.name: The Energy Loop: Huntington and Eccles Canyons Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway (2000)
byways.where: SR-31 from US-89 in Fairview to Huntington, SR-264, SR-96 from Clear Creek to US-6 at Colton, plus (2011) US-6 Colton to Helper and SR-10 to Huntington State Park; Sanpete, Emery and Carbon counties

facts.fact: The route is rich in mining and energy history and includes the recovery site of a 9,500-year-old mammoth skeleton.

The mammoth was found during the rebuilding of Huntington Reservoir Dam and is displayed at the USU Eastern Prehistoric Museum in Price; Skyline Mine still operates along the route, past Electric Lake and Scofield State Park.
Extended February 2, 2011 to include US-6 from Colton to Helper and SR-10 to Huntington State Park.

byways.review: The UDOT layer splits this byway into 'Energy Loop Huntington & Eccles Canyon' plus two 2011 extension rows ('Energy Loop Extension - US-6 from Colton to Helper', 'Energy Loop Extension - SR-31 to Huntington St Pk').

byways.name: Nebo Loop Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway (1998)
byways.where: SR-115 and SR-198 into Payson, then 600 East and Forest Road 015 south to SR-132 east of Nephi; Utah and Juab counties

facts.fact: The road winds between Payson and Nephi across the national forest with views of Mt. Nebo; Devils Kitchen has a half-mile trail to red rock hoodoos, and Payson Lakes lie 12 miles south of Payson.
The road climbs from scrub oak through maple and aspen to fir, spruce and lodgepole pine over 38 miles and is closed in winter.
Mt. Nebo, at 11,928 feet, is the tallest peak in the Wasatch Range.

byways.name: Upper Colorado River Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway (also part of the Dinosaur Diamond National Scenic Byway)
byways.where: SR-128 from US-191 near Moab to the I-70 West Cisco interchange; Grand County

facts.fact: SR-128 begins at the Colorado River bridge north of Moab, follows the river gorge for its first 13 miles, and passes the Fisher Towers under the La Sal Mountains at about mile 24.7.

Castle and Professor valleys were filming locations for westerns including Wagon Master and Rio Grande; the historic Dewey Bridge burned in 2008; the route ends at Cisco, a ghost town founded as a water stop for steam locomotives.

byways.name: Potash-Lower Colorado River Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-279 from US-191 north of Moab to its southwest end at the potash plant; Grand County

facts.fact: SR-279 leaves US-191 4.1 miles north of Moab; climbers work the Wall Street cliffs at about mile 4, petroglyph panels are at mile 5.1, and dinosaur tracks near the Poison Spider trailhead at mile 5.9.
Corona Arch, with an opening of 140 by 105 feet, is reached by trail near mile 9.9; the road ends at the potash mine and its evaporation ponds after 17 miles.

byways.name: Dead Horse Mesa Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway (designated May 16, 2002)
byways.where: SR-313 from US-191 to Dead Horse Point State Park, and the Island in the Sky road to Grand View Point; Grand and San Juan counties

facts.fact: SR-313 leaves US-191 about 9 miles north of Moab; Dead Horse Point overlooks the Colorado River from 2,000 feet above, and the byway continues across the Island in the Sky mesa of Canyonlands to Grand View Point.
Along the road there are views of the La Sal, Abajo and Henry mountains and the Book Cliffs.

byways.review: Rule name is Dead Horse Mesa Scenic Byway; UDOT layer uses 'Dead Horse Point Mesa Scenic Byway'.

byways.name: Indian Creek Corridor Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-211 from US-191 north of Monticello to the Needles District visitor center of Canyonlands National Park; San Juan County

facts.fact: SR-211 begins 14 miles north of Monticello, crosses a high sage plain, and drops through tight turns to Newspaper Rock, a panel of petroglyphs, before following Indian Creek Canyon to the Needles District.
Much of the corridor passes a 5,200-acre ranch protected by The Nature Conservancy, and the route is a well-known climbing area.

byways.name: Bicentennial Highway Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR-95 from SR-24 in Hanksville to US-191 near Blanding; Wayne, Garfield and San Juan counties

facts.fact: Dedicated in 1976 for the national bicentennial, SR-95 replaced a multi-day route of dirt tracks and river ferries; it crosses the Colorado River at Hite and there are no services in the roughly 120 miles between Hanksville and Blanding.
The Henry Mountains to the west were the last range in the lower 48 to be explored and named and hold a free-roaming bison herd.

byways.review: The eastern part of SR-95 (SR-275 to US-191) is also part of the Trail of the Ancients.

byways.name: Trail of the Ancients Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway (2005)
byways.where: SR-95 from SR-275 to US-191, SR-275 to Natural Bridges, US-191 from Blanding to Bluff, and SR-162 to the Colorado line; San Juan County

facts.fact: Ancestral Puebloans occupied this canyon country from about AD 1 to 1300; Ute communities today include White Mesa in Utah.
The route passes Edge of the Cedars State Park Museum in Blanding, Natural Bridges National Monument and Hovenweep National Monument.
The national byway (2005) combines the state byway with the Monument Valley to Bluff byway and the SR-261 and Hovenweep sections of the state scenic backway.

byways.review: The state byway is only the SR-95/SR-275/US-191/SR-162 core; the catalog line is the national byway, which also includes Monument Valley to Bluff, SR-261 (Moki Dugway) and the SR-262 road to Hovenweep, and continues into Colorado.

byways.name: Monument Valley to Bluff Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway (part of the Trail of the Ancients National Scenic Byway)
byways.where: US-163 from the Arizona line to US-191, and US-191 to the Cottonwood Wash bridge in Bluff; San Juan County

facts.fact: From the Arizona border US-163 crosses Monument Valley, reaches Mexican Hat, named for a sombrero-shaped rock nearby, crosses the San Juan River on a historic bridge, and continues to the historic community of Bluff.
Monument Valley is a Navajo Tribal Park.

byways.name: Dinosaur Diamond Prehistoric Highway Scenic Byway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Byway; National Scenic Byway (2002)
byways.where: Utah side: I-70 and Cisco road, SR-128, US-191 Moab to Crescent Junction, I-70 to Green River, US-6 to Helper, US-191 through Indian Canyon to Duchesne, US-40 to the Colorado line; continues in Colorado

facts.fact: The 512-mile loop runs through Moab, Price and Vernal and back through the Colorado towns of Dinosaur, Rangely and Fruita, past Dinosaur National Monument and Price's prehistoric museum.
Several US-40 segments near Naples, Vernal and Ballard have been excluded from the byway by local governments since 2013.
Carbon County suggests starting at the Prehistoric Museum in Price.

byways.name: Bull Creek Pass National Back Country Byway
byways.designation: BLM National Back Country Byway; also a Utah State Scenic Backway

facts.fact: A single-lane dirt road of 68 miles with rough sections, steep grades and blind curves, climbing from desert badlands through spruce and ponderosa to the alpine Bull Creek Pass in the Henry Mountains, where bison, bighorn sheep and pronghorn live.
The byway climbs nearly a mile; allow 6 to 8 hours.

byways.name: Nine Mile Canyon Backway
byways.designation: BLM Back Country Byway; also a Utah State Scenic Backway

facts.fact: Often called 'the world's longest art gallery', the 46-mile canyon holds rock art panels, historic inscriptions and a Fremont village site; visitors usually come from Wellington, south of Price.

The canyon is a major area of the prehistoric Fremont Culture, with petroglyphs, pictographs and cliff granaries; in the 1800s it was used by fur trappers and the army, and iron telegraph poles and settler cabins remain.

byways.name: Pony Express Trail National Back Country Byway
byways.designation: BLM National Back Country Byway; also a Utah State Scenic Backway

facts.fact: A maintained gravel road follows the 1860 to 1861 Pony Express route across Utah's west desert, with station sites and interpretive displays; it starts 25 miles west of Lehi off SR-73.
The byway runs 133 miles, with remains of old stations along the road about every 10 miles.

byways.name: Silver Island Mountains Back Country Byway
byways.designation: BLM National Back Country Byway; also a Utah State Scenic Backway

facts.fact: A 54-mile loop around the Silver Island Mountains that gives access to the Hastings Cutoff of the California Trail, used by the Donner-Reed party in 1846.
The loop starts four miles east of Wendover, beside the Bonneville Salt Flats, with wagon ruts of the California Trail along its north end.

byways.name: Smithsonian Butte National Back Country Byway
byways.designation: BLM National Back Country Byway; also a Utah State Scenic Backway

facts.fact: Runs 9.25 miles between Rockville and Apple Valley, from the Virgin River floodplain through pinyon-juniper to sagebrush at Big Plain Junction, with views of Smithsonian Butte, Eagle Crags and the Zion pinnacles; a side road leads to the ghost town of Grafton, settled in 1861. It becomes impassable in heavy rain.

byways.name: Transcontinental Railroad Back Country Byway
byways.designation: BLM National Back Country Byway; also a Utah State Scenic Backway

facts.fact: The byway follows 90 miles of original hand-built Transcontinental Railroad grade west of Golden Spike National Historical Park, past ghost towns, earthworks, culverts and trestle sites.
It crosses the Great Salt Lake Desert along the Central Pacific grade of 1869 to the Nevada line.

byways.name: Kolob Reservoir Scenic Backway
byways.designation: Utah State Scenic Backway

facts.fact: The backway runs about 45 miles from SR-14 five miles east of Cedar City through aspen forest to Kolob Reservoir and down through meadows into the red and white backcountry of Zion to SR-9; it is closed in winter and not suitable when wet.

issues: No official state web page lists the byways; the canonical list is Utah Admin. Code R926-13 (adminrules.utah.gov returned an empty page to curl, so the rule text was read from Cornell LII, which shows amendments through 4/8/2024).

Visit Utah's scenic byways page counts 28 byways and lists the Alpine Loop (SR-92) as a state byway, but the Alpine Loop is not in R926-13 or in the UDOT layer. It was left out of the state program here and is not in the catalog.
Zion Park Scenic Byway (SR-9, I-15 to US-89) and Morgan-Parleys Scenic Byway (SR-66/SR-65, designated 2017) are in the rule but not in the catalog; both have UDOT layer lines (gisValue set).

Great Salt Lake Legacy Parkway Scenic Byway was renamed Great Salt Lake Scenic Byway and extended in 2018 (to the West Davis Corridor, SR-127 and Antelope Island Marina); the catalog line covers only the 12-mile Legacy Parkway.

Trail of the Ancients catalog line is the national byway (Utah and Colorado, including Monument Valley to Bluff and backway segments on SR-261 and to Hovenweep); the state byway itself is only the SR-95/SR-275/US-191/SR-162 core. Monument Valley to Bluff therefore appears both as its own state member and inside the Trail of the Ancients line.
Indian Canyon Scenic Byway and Upper Colorado River Scenic Byway are both inside the Dinosaur Diamond national byway line; overlapping lines on the map are expected.

The UDOT layer misspells some names: 'Markaquant High Plateau Scenic Byway' (Markagunt), and uses 'Dead Horse Point Mesa', 'Fish Lake', 'Journey Through Time' and 'Indian Creek Scenic Byway' forms. Several features are duplicated (e.g. Dinosaur Diamond, Trail of the Ancients, Provo Canyon).

dinosaurdiamondbyway.com, given in search results as the Dinosaur Diamond's site, now redirects to an unrelated gambling domain; do not link it. dinosaurdiamond.org does not respond. Carbon County's page is used instead.

Utah's 1990 Scenic Backways (about 58 dirt and county roads) are not in R926-13, and no current official list was found; USFS pages still label roads as 'State Scenic Backway'. Only catalog backways are listed here.

No official byway page found for Bear Lake, Great Salt Lake or Morgan-Parleys (url null). scenicbyway12.com returned 403 to both curl and WebFetch; Garfield County's Bryce Canyon Country page is used for Highway 12.

USFS pages for Fishlake, Beaver Canyon, Markagunt, Cedar Breaks and Patchwork Parkway (Fishlake and Dixie national forests) were not found at the new fs.usda.gov/r04 URLs; tourism-office pages are used instead.
Dinosaur Diamond has had several US-40 segments near Naples, Vernal area (Uintah County) and Ballard excluded by local governments (2013, 2015, 2022); the catalog line may still include them.
